podcast.body: Featured on the *Beggar's Banquet* album, this song is recognized as another one of the major and impactful hits in The Rolling Stones' extensive career. "al estrifighter van."

Mick Jagger wrote this song about a 1968 Vietnam War protest at the American Embassy in London. It was released in the United States in the summer of 1968, coinciding with widespread protests across the country. The song became a favorite of diverse protesters, from marchers to radical groups seeking to overthrow the government, and legendary music critic Ralph Gleason noted its "desperation" that endeared it to "hardcore street revolutionaries." "Street Fighting Man is probably as political of a song as the stones ever write and play."

podcast.body: This song was influenced by the misinterpretation of Martha and the Van Dellers' "Dancing in the Street" as a call for rioting during civil rights protests. The Rolling Stones "picked up on" this idea for their own track. "something the rolling stones would pick up on later when they released Street Fighting Man, a song that owes more than a little to the band-auler's classic."
